doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Brushes with Louis Armstrong in Chicago and the Oldham brothers
summary: Hinton and other music-wrapped kids hung around Armstrong's rehearsals; friends like Budd Johnson then played with Armstrong; he did not see Louis much until 1953.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Is this when you met Louie? When did you meet Louie?
I didn‟t really meet him. He saw me there, there was a few of us kids wrapped up in music.

And he saw us. We were always in the way. And Bud Johnson came in and those guys, but I was still on that violin thing. And [unintelligible] Brown had his saxophone and Bud Johnson had come in from Texas with a tenor. And the next thing I knew they were playing with Louis Armstrong, a bunch of wonderful brothers named Oldham brothers. One played bass horn and one played saxophone. And they were doing it with [unintelligible] Randolph a trumpet player that was around Chicago. And that era, I was still hanging with this bass… with this violin until Jolson came through with the thing. So then I don‟t see Louie much at all until 1953 and I am working with Basie. I‟m playing out here and met Katherine and Basie are very dear friends and we live here. And Basie would come over here and hang out with me.
